summary: Added logging and existence checks for login, but introduced credential exposure, user‑enumeration, and weakened JWT validation by accepting expired or unverifiable tokens.

comments.body: Logging the password in clear text exposes sensitive credentials in application logs, creating a security risk if logs are accessed by unauthorized parties.
Returning distinct error messages for "User not found" versus "Incorrect password" enables username enumeration, allowing attackers to discover valid accounts.
Catching ExpiredJwtException and still returning true accepts expired tokens, bypassing token expiry checks and permitting replay attacks.
Accepting any JwtException or IllegalArgumentException as valid causes all malformed or tampered tokens to be accepted, effectively disabling JWT authentication.

summary: Added logging and existence checks to the login endpoint and relaxed JWT validation logic. The changes introduce credential exposure in logs, enable user enumeration, and accept unverifiable tokens, creating security risks.

comments.body: Logging the password in clear text exposes sensitive credentials in application logs, which can be accessed by unauthorized users or retained longer than intended.
Returning distinct error messages for "User not found" versus "Incorrect password" enables user enumeration, allowing an attacker to discover valid usernames.
Catching JwtException and returning true causes any malformed or tampered token to be accepted, effectively bypassing authentication verification.

summary: The changes add detailed logging and error messages in AuthController, introduce user existence checks, modify JwtValidator to accept tokens even when verification fails, expand clock skew tolerance, and alter the LoginResponse record to include a message field. Several of these adjustments introduce security and compatibility concerns.

comments.body: Logging the password in clear text (LOGGER.warn with request.password()) writes credentials to application logs, creating a risk of credential leakage and non‑compliance with security best practices.
Returning different error messages for "User not found" versus "Incorrect password" enables user enumeration, allowing an attacker to discover valid usernames based on the response content.
The catch block for JwtException and IllegalArgumentException logs a warning but then returns true, effectively accepting any malformed or tampered token, which defeats token authentication entirely.
Allowing a clock‑skew window of 24 hours is excessively permissive and can let expired or compromised tokens remain valid for an unreasonably long period, increasing the attack surface.
Changing the LoginResponse record to include a second 'message' field modifies the API contract, potentially breaking existing clients that expect only a 'token' field in the JSON response.

summary: Introduces InvalidTaskException, adds title validation in TaskService and a controller exception handler, and updates tests accordingly.

comments.body: Calling task.title() without first checking if the Task argument is null can cause a NullPointerException, leading to 500 errors instead of a controlled Bad Request.
The maximum title length is a hard‑coded magic number; extracting it to a configurable property would improve flexibility and maintainability.

summary: Adds custom InvalidTaskException, title validation in TaskService, and an exception handler in TaskController with corresponding tests.

comments.body: The @ExceptionHandler method is package‑private; while Spring can invoke it, making it public improves readability and aligns with typical controller method visibility.

summary: Introduced InvalidTaskException and added title validation with length limit in TaskService, plus controller exception handling and corresponding tests.

comments.body: validateTitle(task) is called before checking whether the task ID exists, causing a BadRequest error for an invalid title even when the task is not found; this changes the expected 404 response to 400 and can leak validation details for non‑existent resources.

summary: Added project management API with in‑memory repository, service, controller, DTOs and tests.

comments.body: The repository assigns IDs using nextId.getAndIncrement() without ensuring the generated ID is greater than any existing manually‑set IDs, which can cause duplicate keys and overwrite existing projects.

summary: Added project CRUD functionality with in‑memory repository, service, controller, and tests.

comments.body: Sorting projects by id assumes every stored Project has a non‑null id. If a Project with a null id were present (e.g., saved before ID assignment), Comparator.comparing(Project::id) will throw a NullPointerException, causing the whole operation to fail.

summary: Introduces project domain classes, an in‑memory repository, service layer, REST controller, request records and comprehensive unit tests for the new functionality.

comments.body: Potential NullPointerException: the filter uses project.name().equalsIgnoreCase(name) without checking if the stored project's name is null, which could crash if a Project with a null name exists.
